findings.note: GAP LANE, code only, no overlay row (gap lines engine report:7 and verify:55). The reader is src/rules/companions.ts familiarAbilityBudget, which now adds familiarFeatRaise(): +2 when the character owns enhanced-familiar (AoN feat-4717 "You can select four familiar or master abilities each day, instead of two."), +4 when it owns incredible-familiar or incredible-familiar-familiar-master (feat-5004 "a base of six ... instead of four"; prerequisite Enhanced Familiar, so the two are never summed). Additive extras stay on top per the witch and wizard Specials: familiar 2->4, familiar-master-dedication 2->4, familiar-witch 3->5, improved-familiar-attunement 3->5, emissary-familiar 4->6, growthLevels unchanged. src/rules/companionGrants.ts gains CompanionGrant.enhancedFamiliar: 'baked' for draconic-familiar (feat-8093), enhanced-psychopomp-familiar (feat-3471), adaptive-mask-familiar (feat-1104) and incredible-familiar-familiar-master (feat-8005), which print the raised number themselves; 'not-a-familiar' for pet, friend-of-the-sea, pirates-pet; 'unsettled' for psychopomp-familiar, basic-witchcraft, undead-familiar, enhanced-undead-familiar, glyph-familiar, which keep the number they shipped with pending owner question enhanced-familiar#fixed-budget-grants (work/.bP02-queue.json). The shaman grant goes 4 -> 2 because AoN practice-4 hands Enhanced Familiar over at 2nd and Incredible Familiar at 9th (FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS_LEVELED already does), so it reads 2 / 4 / 6 on the printed levels instead of a flat 4. src/sheet/CompanionsTab.tsx appends 'Your <feat> feat raises the number you choose to N.' to the static grant note so it no longer contradicts the 'of N chosen' chip. Pinned by test/batchP02-gap-engine.test.tsx on built wizard / witch / animist-shaman characters and a rendered CompanionsTab.

GAP LANE, code only, no overlay row (gap lines engine report:8 and verify:56). src/rules/attachments.ts: isAttachable(item, character?) accepts a consumable with consumableType 'scroll' only when character.feats owns 'strikers-scroll' (AoN feat-9059 "You can attach a scroll to your weapon or handwraps of mighty blows"); attachHostTypes gives a scroll only 'weapon' (handwraps-of-mighty-blows is itemType weapon); attachKind gains 'scroll', and planAffix refuses a scroll on a host holding a talisman and a talisman on a host holding a scroll, BEFORE the Talismanic Sage cap ("you can't have both a talisman and scroll attached"), while the sage cap still counts talismans only; one scroll per host through the existing one-per-kind rule; planAttach and canAttachTo thread the character. The UI gates pass it: src/sheet/InventoryTab.tsx (draggingAttachable, attachPlanNow) and src/sheet/ItemEditorModal.tsx (AttachmentsSection gets a character prop; its candidate list calls canAttachTo(def, hostAs, character)).
